title: KV Shadow Harmonizer: batch-aware eviction orchestration to reduce GPU fragmentation
creator: Marina Patel
description: Motivation: We observe intermittent GPU memory fragmentation during sustained continuous-batching workloads. This leads to suboptimal KV cache utilization, increased token rehydration, and occasional request tail latency spikes under memory pressure. The KV Shadow Harmonizer is an allocation-and-eviction orchestration layer designed to: 1) maintain a compact live-slot view using lightweight shadow mappings, 2) align eviction decisions with ongoing batch affinity to avoid repeated cache thrash, and 3) proactively reclaim micro-fragments via low-impact background rewrites.
description_details: High-level approach: (a) Shadow mapping: maintain a thin mapping table (shadow map) that groups KV entries into logical segments by access-affinity and sequence-length class. The shadow map does not move large token payloads—only metadata. (b) Batch-aware eviction windows: when a request batch arrives, the orchestrator marks batch-affine shadow segments as protected for the batch's critical path TTL, prioritizing eviction candidates that are both low-recent-use and have low future-batch affinity. (c) Thermal-aware micro-reclamation: background worker probes contiguous low-affinity segments and issues in-place micro-rewrites that consolidate adjacent free slots without a full compaction pause. (d) Admission and resizing: new large sequences are admitted into reserved transient pools if fragmentation heuristics predict high placement failure on main pools.
heuristics_and_signals: Signals used: per-key access recency, batch-origin affinity score, token sequence length bucket, allocation age, GPU free-run percentage, and contiguous-slot-run-length from allocator telemetry. Heuristics combine LRU-like weight with a batch-affinity multiplier and a fragmentation penalty. Score = recency_weight * recency + affinity_multiplier * affinity_score - frag_penalty * small_contiguous_run_count. We cap eviction churn by requiring a delta_threshold before moving hot entries.
implementation_notes: Runtime integration points: - Hook into continuous-batcher admission pipeline to tag incoming requests with affinity tokens. - Shadow map stored as a compact on-GPU structure with periodic CPU mirror for analytics. - Background micro-rewrites use a cooperative scheduling primitive so they yield when tail-latency SLOs are at risk. - Fall back to standard slab eviction when shadow map indicates high churn or worker backlog grows beyond threshold.
sim_results: Synthetic workload simulation (mix of chat + long-context reranking, token distribution matching production 95th-percentile): - Baseline (current allocator): fragmentation index 0.42, cache miss rate 11.4%, tail-99 latency 320ms. - With Shadow Harmonizer (alpha config): fragmentation index 0.33 (-21%), cache miss rate 8.9% (-22%), tail-99 latency 280ms (-12%). Memory overhead: shadow map ~1.6% of KV memory. CPU worker utilization increased by ~4% but bounded by the cooperative scheduler.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature-flagged alpha rollout on a small dedicated pool (canary) with read-only shadow mapping enabled. 2) Enable batch-annotation in serving path and compare telemetry for 48h. 3) Enable micro-rewrite worker in soft mode (limit 1 rewrite/sec/node). 4) Expand to 10% of fleet and run 7-day soak. 5) Full rollout with dynamic thresholds and opt-out per-customer for Private deployments.
observability_and_metrics: Telemetry to add: shadow_map_fill_ratio, micro_rewrite_count, micro_rewrite_latency_histogram, eviction_candidate_score_histogram, batch_affinity_protected_secs, fragmentation_index, kv_cache_miss_rate_by_sequence_bucket. Dashboards/alerts: fragmentation_index > 0.5 for 15m, micro_rewrite_backlog > 100, delta(cache_miss_rate) > +3% vs baseline.
tasks: - Design shadow map schema and GPU layout (Luis). - Implement batch-affinity tagging in batcher (SRE/Batching team). - Implement eviction score function and tie to allocator (Luis + Asha). - Add micro-rewrite worker and cooperative scheduler hook (Sanjay). - Add telemetry + dashboards (Observability). - Run synthetic soak and compare against baseline (QA).
acceptance_criteria: - Production-like soak shows fragmentation index reduction >= 15% without increasing average latency. - Cache miss rate decreases or remains within 1% of baseline. - Micro-rewrite worker does not cause ASG scale-ups or violate per-node tail-latency SLO. - Rollout can be toggled off via feature flag with no data loss.
risks_and_mitigation: Risks: shadow map inconsistency during node failover, worker-induced latency spikes, misclassification of batched affinity leading to unnecessary protection. Mitigations: lightweight epoch-based versioning for shadow map, cooperative yield and backpressure for workers, conservative default affinity thresholds and telemetry-driven tuning.
